plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Exit METU to reduce high-beta software exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to lower income concentration.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce broad index exposure.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by cutting leverage and reducing concentration.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for low drawdowns and capital preservation. Expect modest returns around 1.5% per month, with a focus on stability over aggressive growth. Risk is minimized by cutting leverage and holding cash.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to minimal levels.
Reduce METU exposure to 3% to manage high-beta software risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to rebalance broad index exposure.
Buy TZA at 4% to add a hedge against broad market declines.
This balanced approach seeks risk-first growth by trimming leverage and adding a defensive position.
A moderate cash buffer will be maintained.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly returns with a risk-first approach. It reduces leverage and concentration while adding a defensive ETF. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate, with a focus on preserving capital while seeking growth.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to 6% each.
Increase high-beta software METU to 6%.
Trim SPY to 15% to reduce broad index exposure.
Buy SOXS at 5% to add a short position in semiconductors.
This aggressive plan aims for high growth by concentrating leverage and high-beta names.
A smaller cash buffer is maintained, and stops will be strictly managed.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets approximately 4% monthly returns by leaning into leverage and concentrated tech/semiconductor exposure. Expect significantly higher potential upside but also much larger potential drawdowns due to leverage and leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MSFU, MUU, PLTU) and high-beta software (METU) to zero.
Increase QQQI to 30% to enhance income generation.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and capital preservation.
Leverage is eliminated, and focus shifts to income-producing assets.
A cash buffer will be maintained to support income generation.
This strategy aims for low drawdowns and reliable income over growth.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly returns through steady distributions. It prioritizes capital preservation and reliable income by eliminating leverage and high-beta names, focusing on income ETFs. While distributions are prioritized, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
